title: La Mole, valley, La Verne dam and a discreet village
author: Caramagnols
excerpt: La Mole reveals another face of the gulf, more rural and more linked to water. The valley, the La Verne dam and the modest scale of the village give the walk a distinctive tone.
content:
La Mole does not attract through the immediate effect of a harbour or a hill village. Its interest is quieter. One has to look at the valley, stored water, meadows, slopes and the way the settlement holds within this landscape.

A commune on the valley floor

In La Mole, relief frames the view instead of opening it immediately towards the sea. This valley position gives the walk a more inward, more rural and often calmer rhythm.

The La Verne dam as a major landmark

The dam recalls the very concrete role of water in this sector. It is not only a point of interest, but an element that structures the reading of the commune between resources, landscape and uses.

Why discretion is the quality here

La Mole does not try to impress. That is precisely what makes it interesting within the gulf dossier. It shows a territory of passage and valley, where one better understands what the shoreline owes to its inland support.
